core_obligations: Consider the set T_of closed subschemes T' of T with P(T'), and extract a minimal element T' using the limit assumption (proof lines 17067-17069): by assumption (2) applied to nested chains, a minimal T' exists.

Show T' is reduced by the thickening assumption (proof line 17070): the reduction of T' is a thickening, and P is invariant under thickenings, so P is inherited by the reduction, contradicting minimality unless T' is already reduced.

Pick the generic point eta = Spec(K) of an irreducible component of T' and write eta = lim V over the affine opens V containing eta (proof lines 17071-17073); the minimality of T' plus assumption (3) force P(V) for each such V (proof lines 17074-17075), and assumption (2) then gives P(eta) (proof line 17076).
proof_roadmap: Minimal closed subscheme T' with P(T') by Zorn via (2).
T' reduced via the thickening invariance (1).
For eta = Spec(K), the generic point of an irreducible component, any affine open V around eta with P(V) holds by (3) and minimality; apply the limit property (2) to conclude P(eta).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the formal device by which the chapter reduces properties of schemes to properties over fields (statement lines 17045-17063). The proof's content is the minimality argument: one takes a minimal closed subscheme T' with P, deduces it is reduced from the thickening invariance (proof lines 17067-17070), and then applies the third assumption to the affine open neighbourhoods V of an irreducible component's generic point and the second assumption to their limit, obtaining P(Spec(K)) (proof lines 17074-17076). H2: the argument is a short chain of standard reductions, not a long construction.
